It was a mixed week on Wall Street as bond yields continue to climb.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports mortgage rates rose more than 7 percent.
Mortgage rates are closely tied to the yield on 10-year treasuries, which jump to their highest
level in more than two decades this week. Bondholders are demanding higher returns in
response to stubborn inflation, a ballooning federal debt, and competing demand for credit
from big tech companies that are shoveling lots of money into artificial intelligence.
On Friday, the Labor Department delivered a weaker-than-expected jobs report,
showing U.S. employers added just 29,000 jobs last month. Investors now think it's less likely
the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates when policymakers meet later this month.
For the week the Dow fell, one and a quarter percent, the S&P 500 index slipped by a quarter

Zambia once imported almost all of its fertilizer. Creating its own became a food security issue.

Zambian farmers like Kanangwenulov have turned to Bokashi, a fermented compost method popularized
